text:
sara: Heads up — EU customer (acme-corp) reporting random 403s + long tail latency since ~09:40 UTC. Started right after the regional CNAME swap to APAC. Billing spike flagged. Posting logs.

leo: @sara can you paste a curl and the X-Region / x-edge headers? Also which resolver they're on?

sara: here's a curl from their VM (eu cloud provider):

curl -I https://api.redwood.example.com -H 'Host: api.redwood.example.com'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-redwood-region: us-east-1
x-request-id: ab12cd

They report RTT ~480ms.

raj: dig +trace from a few vantage points shows mixed answers — some resolvers seeing apac cname, others legacy eu. sample:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.redwood.example.com A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example.com. 300 IN CNAME apac-01.redwood.net.
apac-01.redwood.net. 60 IN A 3.120.45.10
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood.net. 60 IN NS ns1.redwood.net.
```
And from eu resolver:
```
api.redwood.example.com. 86400 IN CNAME eu-legacy.redwood.net.
eu-legacy.redwood.net. 86400 IN A 18.200.60.20
```

maria: sounds like we rolled CNAME but TTLs on legacy records were high; some ISPs still have old cached records -> cross-region hits causing token validation failures (signing keys bound to region). Also maybe IPv6-only resolvers returning different chain.

leo: confirm AAAA chain? If IPv6 returns eu-legacy AAAA while A returns apac, clients might pick IPv6 and land in eu-legacy -> mismatch. Can you get dig AAAA +short from affected client resolver?

raj: got it, here's AAAA from their resolver:
```
# from client resolver
api.redwood.example.com. 86400 IN CNAME eu-legacy.redwood.net.
eu-legacy.redwood.net. 86400 IN AAAA 2a0c:dead:beef::20
```
But public caches show apac AAAA too. Split-view / stale caches.

maria: mitigation options: (1) add temporary region-aware header fallback that accepts old signing key for 'eu-legacy' for 24h, (2) lower new CNAME TTL and push purge via our dns-sync to partners, (3) ask customer to restart DNS/cache on client side as stop-gap.

sara: customer asked for repro steps to send to their infra: 1) dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood.example.com ANY +short 2) curl -I with Host header 3) ping/traceroute to answer IP. I'll share.

leo: I'll open a quick runbook task. @raj can you run sync/purge to major ISP caches (cloudflare/major-dns) and set apac CNAME TTL=60 for 1h? @maria please add temporary acceptance of eu-legacy signing key (auth fallback) to edge config.

raj: started dns-sync job 3612345700 -> pushed shorter TTL. Not all upstreams support purge. Wrote note to ops: 'ISP caches may obey original 86400 until TTL expires.'


dns-bot: deploy:region-cname-swap apac rollout at 3612345600 by deploy-bot (success)

sara: thanks team. Customer notified, asking for ETA on full resolution. I'll follow up with billing team to review the spike. Filing support-ESCL ticket.
